## D — Accuracy notes and source flags: sign colors and shapes, regulatory, warning, construction and guide signs, dark signals and gridlock
Every C and C2 fact cites exactly one physical manual page from the selected range; nothing relies on outside knowledge.
Every sign on these pages is shown as a picture; the dossier uses only the printed caption text and does not describe sign shapes, symbols or colors beyond what the text states [A01].
The work zone fine on the construction sign page applies when workers are present, while the work zone paragraph in the sharing the road chapter states the fine as an add-on to the regular ticket without that condition; the dossier keeps each wording on its own page (verify MN-SIGNSA-D-WORKZONE) [A09].
The dark signal rule is stated exactly as printed, treating the intersection as uncontrolled; it is flagged for confirmation of the wording the written test expects (verify MN-SIGNSA-D-DARKSIGNAL) [A10].
Route sign markers for interstate, U.S., Minnesota and county roads are pictures; only their names are recorded.
The image-based sign recognition skill is declared as needing a dedicated surface built from official sign artwork, not from this text.

corpus_stability.reason: The Minnesota Driver’s Manual prints a single edition line (June 2026) on its front cover and opens with a New laws and information chapter that collects recent changes in one place, with no sign of more than one rewrite per year in the selected pages.

verification_debt.claim_text: On physical page 67 the Minnesota Driver's Manual (June 2026) says work zone speeding is fined $300 when workers are present, while physical page 57 says work zone speeding fines are $300 in addition to the regular speeding ticket with no workers-present condition; confirm the current rule against an official DPS source.

On physical page 68 the Minnesota Driver's Manual (June 2026) says a traffic signal that is not functioning should be treated as an uncontrolled intersection; confirm against an official DPS or DVS source that this is the treatment the written test expects before learner items are finalized.
